title: How a fission chain reaction releases energy
examples: How does a nuclear chain reaction work?
Why does splitting an atom release energy?

stages.label: Slow neutron
stages.note: A slow neutron is absorbed by a uranium-235 nucleus.
stages.ask: Why does the neutron need to be slow?

stages.label: Nucleus wobbles
stages.note: The nucleus becomes unstable and stretches like a wobbling drop.

stages.label: It splits in two
stages.note: It splits into two smaller nuclei, called fission products.
stages.ask: What are fission products?

stages.label: Energy released
stages.note: The fragments fly apart fast, heating the fuel.
stages.ask: Where does the energy in fission come from?

stages.label: Two or three neutrons
stages.note: Each split also frees two or three new neutrons.

stages.label: More splits
stages.note: If one of them splits another nucleus, the chain goes on.
stages.ask: What is a chain reaction?

explain.say: Uranium-235 has a nucleus so large that it is only just stable. When it absorbs a slow neutron, the nucleus wobbles and splits into two smaller nuclei.

faq.q: Why does the neutron need to be slow?
faq.a: Uranium-235 captures slow neutrons far more easily than fast ones, a bit like a slow ball being easier to catch. Reactors use a moderator, such as water or graphite, to slow down the fast neutrons from fission.

faq.q: Where does the energy in fission come from?
faq.a: The fragments together weigh slightly less than the original nucleus and neutron. That tiny missing mass becomes energy, as Einstein's E equals m c squared describes, and because c is huge, a little mass makes a lot of energy.
asks: Why does splitting atoms release energy?

faq.a: It is a reaction in which each step sets off the next. In fission, neutrons freed by one split go on to split more nuclei, so the process keeps itself going.
asks: How does a chain reaction keep going?

faq.q: Why is uranium-235 used and not uranium-238?
faq.a: Uranium-235 splits readily when it catches a slow neutron, but uranium-238, the common form, usually just absorbs it without splitting. Only about 0.7 percent of natural uranium is uranium-235.

They are the smaller atoms left after a nucleus splits, such as barium and krypton, or caesium and strontium. Many are radioactive, which is why used nuclear fuel must be stored safely for a long time.

facts: Each fission of a uranium-235 nucleus releases about 200 million electronvolts of energy.
Fission was discovered in 1938 by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann and explained by Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch.

quiz.say: In a reactor running steadily, how many neutrons from each fission go on, on average, to cause another fission?
quiz.show: Neutrons per fission causing a new fission, in a steady reactor?
quiz.why: With exactly one, each generation of fissions is the same size, so the heat output stays steady.

wrong.1: With none, the chain dies out and the reactor shuts down.
wrong.2: If all went on, the reaction would grow quickly; reactors are designed to prevent this.
